title: Run the Velora admin panel on Cloudflare staging and fix auth/API at the root

root_cause.why_not_the_api: the kernel's own 404 is {"status":"error","error":{"code":"NOT_FOUND","requestId":"<uuid>"}} (apps/api/src/kernel/server.ts); the observed envelope is a platform envelope and carries no requestId from the API
root_cause.why_it_happened: apps/web/next.config.ts rewrote /api/:path* at BUILD time to VELORA_API_ORIGIN, which in the deployed bundle was https://velora-modern-staging.up.railway.app (see apps/web-edge-cf/wrangler.jsonc). That host no longer exists, so no API was ever reached
root_cause.fix_direction: give the API a Cloudflare origin (apps/api-cf) and route /api/* to it at REQUEST time from a route handler

first_admin_gap.finding: There is no self-service or ops path to create the FIRST admin account. Every route that could create an admin requires an authenticated admin; the System Owner bootstrap (POST ownership claim) requires the acting row to already be role='admin' AND email-verified AND active; registration creates an unverified 'normal' user and email delivery is the LogMailProvider (nothing sent) on this Worker.
first_admin_gap.consequence: The panel is deployed, gated and reachable, but nobody can log into it until an admin row exists in the staging database.
unblock_options_owner_side: an existing admin whose password the owner holds (the owner reported none)

DB-level provisioning by the owner (Neon staging credentials): insert/update a users row with role='admin', status='active', email_verified_at set, and a password_hash produced by the app's own VeloraHasher so the password policy is not bypassed
a reviewed ops script that does the above with the app's own hasher (not written here — it creates an account, which is an owner decision)
first_admin_gap.not_done_on_purpose: no account, password, token or role was invented; nothing was written to the staging database

resolved.how: owner authorised a database-level provisioning; the password hash was produced by the app's own VeloraHasher (Argon2id, ADR-005 parameters) and the row carries role='admin', status='active', email_verified_at=now()
resolved.tool: a single-use local script (velora-ops/admin-provision/provision.mts) using the owner's Neon key; it refuses to run if any admin already exists, and the deployed credential it replaced was removed — no admin-minting endpoint exists on Cloudflare
resolved.audit_note: no audit_log row was written for the provisioning itself: that table's action vocabulary is CHECK-constrained and actor_user_id is NOT NULL. The first real audit rows are the admin's own actions (USER_STATUS_CHANGED, actor 11)

workers_hashing_bug.symptom: POST /api/v1/auth/register → 500 INTERNAL; login could not have rehashed either
workers_hashing_bug.cause: VeloraHasher uses hash-wasm, which the Workers runtime refuses: 'WebAssembly.compile(): Wasm code generation disallowed by embedder'. needsRehash() sends every successful bcrypt login through hash() too, so BOTH credential paths were broken while every other route looked healthy
workers_hashing_bug.fix: apps/api-cf/src/workersHasher.ts — Argon2id in pure TypeScript (@noble/hashes/argon2.js) producing the identical $argon2id$v=19$m=19456,t=2,p=1$… encoding, bcryptjs for $2a/$2b/$2y, constant-time compare, parameters read from each hash so a future cost bump still verifies old credentials
workers_hashing_bug.proof: apps/api-cf/src/workersHasher.test.ts (6 tests): Worker→Node and Node→Worker verification both directions, identical encoded shape, bcrypt incl. Legacy $2y$, foreign/malformed hashes refused; plus a live register on staging returning 201 and a live admin login returning 200
